correctness.rationale: A selected arc set is a multipath exactly when outdegree and indegree are at most one at every vertex and no directed cycle occurs. Independent enumeration by arc subsets of sizes <=5 and by outgoing-choice partial permutations agreed, obtaining 714 nonempty faces with f-vector (18,108,264,252,72). The explicit 18-coordinate toggle pairing yields 341 disjoint face pairs and one critical vertex, 19 critical dimension-three cells and 12 critical dimension-four cells; the fully reversed 2376-incidence Hasse digraph was independently topologically sorted as a DAG. Independently implemented exact signed unit-pivot integer elimination gave zero residual 12-to-19 Morse boundary. The remaining CW has no critical one/two cells; by simple-connectivity and Hurewicz, its 4-cell attaching classes are measured by the zero degrees in pi3 of the 19-S3 wedge, yielding the asserted integral wedge, not merely homology. The complete finite census is exhaustive for precisely six vertices.
residual_risks: Only the exact fully bidirected six-vertex digraph, not one-way orientations, is proved.

evidence: Caputi 2026 Theorem 2.10 addresses bidirected polygonal digraphs; Resultary 2026 double stars have underlying trees with no three-by-three complete bipartite cycles.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither a polygon theorem nor the two-hub tree family has hypotheses containing the fully bidirected K3,3 case, and no graph reduction is provided to imply the given wedge.

originality.rationale: Caputi et al 2022 Theorem 3.7 concerns the one-way complete bipartite digraph with only arcs from V to W, not the eighteen-arc fully bidirected object; Caputi et al 2026 addresses bidirected polygons and constructions; the published bidirected double-star result concerns a tree and cannot specialize to K3,3. Matching and ordinary Morse complexes of K3,3 are different face posets. No covering entry located by actual Resultary searches or inspected primary texts; qualified priority only.

value.rationale: A natural first balanced fully bidirected bipartite case with several interlocking directed cycles gives a nontrivial mixed-dimensional integral homotopy classification; exact attaching maps matter beyond a Betti table, and the case is a meaningful boundary not arbitrary numeric slicing.
residual_risks: This is a finite natural case; its interest rests on natural balanced directed-cycle interactions and full homotopy information, not any asserted general formula.

final_claim: The integral homotopy type of the multipath complex of the fully bidirected K_{3,3} digraph with 18 arcs is the wedge of 19 three-spheres and 12 four-spheres.
